title: Data minimization & telemetry messaging for enterprise evaluations
content:
Purpose:
This brief provides recommended messaging, customer Q&A, and a mapping of evidence artifacts focused on two pressure points we see in enterprise RFPs: 1) telemetry / audit-log transparency and 2) data minimization across hosted, dedicated, and private modes.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: AE/CSEs responding to procurement and security questionnaires (SOC2, ISO, HIPAA)
- Secondary: Documentation owners (privacy, infra, product) who will need to surface artifacts
- Scope: high-level claims + implementation notes (what to show in an evidence folder), plus canned lines for sales and CSEs.

Executive positioning (3 short pillars):
1) Predictable control over what we collect: telemetry is scoped to operational signals (latency, errors, usage metrics) and per-customer request metadata needed for debugging and SLAs; customer payloads are not used for model telemetry unless explicitly opted in.
2) Minimal-by-default retention: default retention windows for telemetry are short (30 days for detailed debug logs, 90 days aggregated), with configurable retention/disable options in Dedicated and Private.
3) Audit-first evidence: we provide audit-ready extracts (immutable audit-log exports, tamper-evident event sequences, KMS-wrapped keys) aligned to SOC2 control objectives and HIPAA audit requirements.

Key talking points (short lines for sellers):
- "We only capture telemetry required to operate and secure inference: request timestamps, model ID/variant, routing decision, error codes, and resource usage. We do not index customer prompt content for product analytics unless the customer opts in."
- "For Dedicated and Private deployments, teams can disable tenant-level telemetry collection entirely or direct telemetry to customer-owned sinks (S3, GCS, SIEM)."
- "Audit logs are exportable in vendor-neutral formats and include cryptographic checksums when requested for high-assurance customers."

Competitor gap analysis (what buyers worry about / where competitors slip):
- Competitor A (managed-hosted): strong marketing on "observability" but retains raw request logs for longer and uses aggregated prompts for model improvement without clear opt-out.
- Competitor B (self-hosted runtime): claims full control but lacks built-in tamper-resistant audit export and requires heavy ops integration for retention policies.
- Competitor C (API-first provider): good SOC2 paperwork but weak on customer-side evidence (no per-request immutable IDs or easy forensic exports).

How Redwood differentiates (concrete capabilities to call out):
- Opt-in model-improvement telemetry with explicit contract language (no training on customer data by default).
- Configurable retention and routing for telemetry (customer sinks + per-tenant toggles).
- Audit export bundle: per-request metadata CSV, KV-cache footprints, routing decisions, and a signed manifest (useful for legal/forensic reviews).
- KMS/HSM integration for key wrapping and evidence of key access events.

Evidence map for a typical SOC2/ISO/RFP ask (what to include in a deliverable zip):
- Controls matrix (link to SOC2 control mappings) + responsible owners
- Sample immutable audit-log export (one week) in JSONL & CSV with README explaining fields
- Retention policy docs showing default and configurable windows
- Telemetry schema: list of collected fields, sampling rules, and aggregation logic
- Opt-in form example for model-improvement telemetry and signed customer consent template
- Architecture diagram highlighting Dedicated/Private telemetry routing options and where customer-owned sinks appear
- KMS access logs (example) and HSM certificate references for customers requesting hardware-backed keys

HIPAA-specific notes (brief):
- Treat PHI as customer data: Redwood will not process PHI for model improvement unless a BAA and explicit opt-in are in place; default is no training on PHI.
- Provide per-request provenance: request IDs, processing node IDs, and storage location tags to support forensic and breach analysis.
- For Private on-prem deployments, recommend a configuration checklist for customer to ensure PHI never leaves the environment (network policies, egress filters, and disabled telemetry sinks).

Sample canned Q&A (for AE/CSE):
Q: "Do you keep customer prompts for analysis?"
A: "No — prompts are not used for product analytics or model training by default. We store limited request metadata for routing/observability; customers can opt in to contribute content for improvement with documented consent and controls."

Q: "Can we get raw audit log exports for a security incident?"
A: "Yes — we provide immutable JSONL exports with timestamps, request IDs, model variant, route, error codes, and checksums. For Dedicated customers we can ship logs to your SIEM in real time."

Q: "How do you demonstrate non-repudiation of audit logs?"
A: "We can provide signed manifests and cryptographic hashes over exported sequences. For high-assurance customers we support KMS-wrapped signing keys and periodic attestation snapshots."

Suggested contractual language snippets (short, for CSEs & legal):
- "Provider will not use Customer Content to improve models or derive product analytics unless Customer explicitly opts in via a separate written agreement."
- "Provider will retain operational telemetry for X days by default; Dedicated/Private customers may configure retention to meet their compliance needs."

Implementation notes for product/infra (for follow-up):
- Add a feature flag to fully disable request-body capture per-tenant and validate via automated tests and a telemetry audit job.
- Implement export manifest signer backed by KMS; store signatures with export metadata.
- Provide example Terraform to wire Dedicated telemetry to a customer-owned S3/GCS sink.

Next actions (owners):
- Create an "audit bundle" template and store in compliance artifacts (Owner: Lena) — due 2024-12-15
- Add opt-in consent template to legal playbook and link from onboarding (Owner: Samir) — due 2025-01-10
- Engineering spike to add per-tenant body-capture toggle + automated verification (Owner: infra-serving-runtime) — PR by 2025-02-01

Appendix: short glossary for sales (one-liners):
- Telemetry: operational signals (latency, errors, routing) used to run and debug the service.
- Audit log: immutable sequence of events tied to requests and configuration changes, exportable for forensics.
- Opt-in telemetry: explicit customer consent to allow request content to be used for product improvement.

Bottom line (two sentences):
Enterprises buy predictability. Lead with control (disable by default), evidence (exportable signed logs), and configurable routing (customer sinks + Dedicated/Private options) — that combination closes the most security/RFP gaps we see today.
